description:
Approved by the user 2026-11-17 (relayed verbatim by Bugs and Cleanup: "do so; we'll want to recheck the current fixtures to ensure that we use this feature where possible.").

Bug: fz rejects
  def convert(n) do String.to_integer(n) rescue e in ArgumentError -> {:error, e.message} end
on every path with error[parse/invalid-function-definition]: `def` function clause must have exactly one `do` body (quoted_surface.rs:729 clause_group_key -> is_single_do_keyword). Elixir 1.19 accepts it.

Elixir: elixir_def.erl:241-253 def_to_clauses. A body of exactly [do: B] stays B; any other keyword list containing do becomes {:try, [definition: Kind | Meta], [Keywords]}, so do/rescue/catch/else/after become an ordinary try's options, validated by elixir_clauses:'try'/4. definition: Kind lets diagnostics say def instead of try. Each clause wraps only its body; args and guards stay outside.

Change: clause_group_key accepts a def/defp/defmacro/defmacrop body whose keyword list is do plus only rescue/catch/else/after, rewritten into a try node for decode_try (quoted_function.rs:884) so validation is shared. Bodyless and unknown-key (nope:) bodies keep today's error (compiler2_test.rs:1424 pins them). Check quoted_function.rs's body decode for a second single-do assumption.

Fixture: oracle: self, a multi-clause def using rescue, catch, else and after with a guarded clause, all three paths; plus an error fixture for an implicit-try-only refusal (e.g. else without rescue/catch) if diagnostics name def.

Acceptance: three paths agree with Elixir; pinned refusals unchanged; full gate.
title: A function body may carry rescue, catch, else and after, as an implicit try
